solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Scotland not getting its own back in Balkan country

indicators.note: something going back runs the wrong way, so the short word is read from right to left
failing to get something means it is left out, so letters are taken away from the longer word

parts.note: the country on the Adriatic whose capital is Tirana
the little word from the clue itself, turned round

explanation.surface: Scotland fails to take revenge on a Balkan nation it has some quarrel with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Getting its own back' reads as revenge, but 'back' simply turns 'in' round; removing that from ALBANIA leaves ALBA.
explanation.definitionFit: Alba is the Scottish Gaelic name for the country, used on signs and by the national broadcaster.

clue.text: Fitting a rugby player of exceptional size

parts.note: taken as written
a prop is a front-row forward in rugby
OS is the abbreviation for outsize, a clothing size for very large people

explanation.surface: A tailor measures up an enormous rugby player for his kit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fitting' suggests a clothes fitting to go with the outsize player, but it is the definition. OS (outsize) is a standard British clothing label.
explanation.definitionFit: Something apposite or appropriate to the moment is fitting, which is the meaning of this borrowed French word.

clue.text: See rib chops I demolished

indicators.note: a demolished building is knocked apart, so the letters are broken up and rebuilt

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone watches a plate of rib chops being wolfed down by the diner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' looks like an instruction to look, but it is a noun: a see is a bishop's diocese.
explanation.definitionFit: A see is the district or office of a bishop, and bishopric names exactly that territory and post.

clue.text: Bear east of port, coming across a storm

indicators.note: in a clue written across the grid, east means to the right, so one piece follows another

parts.note: Hull is a port city on the Humber estuary in England
taken as written
Baloo is the bear in The Jungle Book

explanation.surface: A bear sails in from the east of a harbour town and stumbles into a gale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bear' looks like a verb meaning endure a storm, but it is a named bear, Baloo, placed after the port.
explanation.definitionFit: A storm can mean an uproar or outcry, as in a storm of protest, which is a noisy commotion.

clue.text: Result of lob?

parts.note: surface reading: what happens after a lofted tennis stroke
setter's reading: a lob is a stroke sent high in the air, so the word for an outcome is split into an upward stroke

explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as two words: a lob is literally a shot that goes up, and the whole word means an outcome.
explanation.definitionFit: The final outcome or consequence of a matter is its upshot, so the result of anything fits.

clue.text: Gents perhaps need whipping, and this one needs tying up!

parts.note: the Gents is a men's lavatory, an example of a loo, and plural here

indicators.note: whipping stirs things into a froth, so the letters are beaten into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Some gentlemen deserve a flogging, and this particular one deserves to be tied up too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gents' reads as men but is the British sign for a men's toilet; 'this one' then points back at the answer itself.
explanation.definitionFit: An unfinished detail is a loose end, and the stock phrase is to tie up loose ends.

clue.text: Mustang, don't peg out now, do you hear? This'll help you breathe!

parts.note: broncho is a variant spelling of bronco, a wild horse like a mustang

indicators.note: asking whether you hear points to what is spoken, so the phrase is to be heard not read

parts.note: to peg out is slang for to die, so not now means later

explanation.surface: A rider urges a wild horse not to collapse and die, offering it an inhaler.
explanation.walkthrough: BRONCHO is the less common spelling of bronco; 'peg out' is British slang for dying.
explanation.definitionFit: A drug that widens the airways of the lungs, such as an asthma inhaler, makes breathing easier.

clue.text: Hear name attached to limerick writer

indicators.note: something attached to another is joined on beside it, so one piece is fixed after the other

parts.note: Edward Lear popularised the limerick in his Book of Nonsense
N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: Someone is told the name of the poet behind a limerick.
explanation.walkthrough: The blocks go on in reverse of clue order: the name letter is attached after the writer.
explanation.definitionFit: To hear of news is to be informed or find it out, a common sense of the verb in 'I learn that...'.

clue.text: Blasted meatloaf finally going brown

indicators.note: the final part going means the closing letter departs from the word
something blasted is blown apart, so the letters are scattered and reset

parts.note: the dish with its last letter removed

explanation.surface: A cursed meatloaf is finally browning in the oven.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blasted' reads as a curse on the meatloaf and 'going brown' as cooking; the answer is a colour, not a food here.
explanation.definitionFit: The name of the ground oats also serves as a colour term for a pale greyish-beige brown shade.

clue.text: Cold such as nothing comes close to

definitions.meaning: first meaning: aloof and unfriendly in manner

definitions.text: such as nothing comes close to

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a description of something so cold nothing will go near it; the two halves are separate senses of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: An unfriendly, standoffish person is hard to get near, and something unmatched cannot be equalled by any rival.

clue.text: Begrudges housing costs around London area

indicators.note: to go around something is to surround it, so one piece encloses another

parts.note: rents are what tenants pay for their homes
SE is the south-east London postcode area

explanation.surface: Someone resents what homes cost in and around London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Housing' looks like the container signal, but it is part of the phrase for rents; 'around' does the enclosing.
explanation.definitionFit: To begrudge someone something is to feel bitter or aggrieved about it, the same as resentment.

clue.text: Tornado converted into Hummer?

indicators.note: converting something turns it into a different form, so the letters take a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A fighter jet is refitted as a big military road vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: Tornado and Hummer both suggest military machines; but to hum is British slang for to smell, so a hummer is something that smells.
explanation.definitionFit: A substance that gives off a smell is an odorant, and in British slang anything that hums stinks.

clue.text: Two Soups, claiming small screen broadcast: critique extremely glowing

definitions.note: a gerund, the act of glowing, standing for the noun

indicators.note: to claim something is to take hold of it, so the outer pieces grasp a letter

parts.note: pho is a Vietnamese noodle soup, taken twice
S is the abbreviation for small

indicators.note: broadcasting originally meant scattering seed widely, so the letters are strewn afresh

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its ends, so only its first and last letters are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: A reviewer raves about a television cookery show featuring two soups.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Small screen' suggests television, but it splits: small is S and screen is the anagram fodder. Pho is the Vietnamese soup.
explanation.definitionFit: Phosphorescence is light given off without heat, as by some sea creatures, which is a steady glowing.

clue.text: Creativity encapsulated by senior European intellectual

indicators.note: something encapsulated is enclosed in a capsule, so one piece sits inside another

parts.note: SR is the abbreviation for senior
art is creative skill
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: An elderly European thinker's creativity is summed up neatly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Senior European intellectual' reads as one phrase describing the answer, but only the last word defines; the rest is wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Jean-Paul Sartre was a French existentialist philosopher and writer, a classic example of a public thinker.

clue.text: Playing well, Arsenal's wingers relaxed

parts.note: a player on good form is said to be in form

indicators.note: wingers play out on the flanks, so only the letters at the two edges are used

parts.note: the first and last letters of the club's name

explanation.surface: The Arsenal wide players are performing well and looking at ease.
explanation.walkthrough: Wingers sound like players, but here they are the outside letters of the word. Arsenal is a London football club.
explanation.definitionFit: Casual, easy-going and without ceremony describes both a relaxed manner and an informal one.

clue.text: Underground no-good creature of myth that will move in time

definitions.note: a relative clause describing the device rather than a noun

indicators.note: without good means the letter standing for good is dropped

parts.note: a metro is an underground railway
a gnome from folklore, minus its G for good

explanation.surface: A wicked mythical beast lurks below ground, biding its time.
explanation.walkthrough: G is the standard abbreviation for good, so 'no-good' removes it from GNOME.
explanation.definitionFit: The ticking device used by musicians swings its arm back and forth at a set tempo, keeping the beat.

clue.text: Have good intentions from humble origin?

parts.note: mean can describe lowly, poor circumstances
a well is a source, as in a wellspring

explanation.surface: Someone from modest beginnings has a kind heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Humble origin' reads as one phrase about background; it is split into two separate words.
explanation.definitionFit: To act with kindly purpose even if the result is poor is the idiom used of well-meaning people.

clue.text: Bloomer from bloke on bike perhaps confusing whereabouts of A&E

indicators.note: one thing sitting on another is placed next to it, so the pieces are joined in sequence
mixing up where the two named letters are kept means they trade places

parts.note: a bike is an example of a cycle
a bloke is British slang for a man

explanation.surface: A cyclist gets lost looking for the hospital emergency department.
explanation.walkthrough: A&E is the British hospital emergency department; here it means the letters A and E swap positions in CYCLEMAN. 'Bloomer' also suggests a blunder.
explanation.definitionFit: The cyclamen is a flowering plant with swept-back petals, and any flowering plant is a bloomer.

clue.text: Back on board, wearing headphones and loose items of clothing

indicators.note: whatever is worn is covered by clothing, so one piece sits inside another

parts.note: cans is slang for headphones
aft is the rear part of a ship

explanation.surface: A passenger returns to the plane with headphones on and wearing baggy garments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back on board' looks like returning to a vehicle; it is the nautical word for the stern area.
explanation.definitionFit: A kaftan or caftan is a long, loose tunic or robe, originally from the Middle East.

clue.text: Two men in Casualty

parts.note: Vic is a man's name, short for Victor
Tim is another man's name

explanation.surface: Two male characters appear in the hospital drama Casualty.
explanation.walkthrough: Casualty is a long-running BBC hospital drama, which makes the capital look like a title; here it simply means someone hurt.
explanation.definitionFit: A person injured or killed in an accident or attack is both a casualty and a victim.

clue.text: MPs set for reshuffle to accommodate ego trip?

indicators.note: accommodating a guest means giving it room inside, so one piece lodges within another
a cabinet reshuffle moves people into new posts, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written
ego is the Latin for I, the self

explanation.surface: Politicians awaiting a government reshuffle indulge their vanity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ego trip' reads as a single phrase, but it splits: ego is the letter I and trip is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A stumble or a slip-up is both a trip and a misstep, literally or figuratively.

clue.text: Speck, among foremost of Europe's smoked hams

indicators.note: to be among things is to sit in their midst, so one piece goes between others
the foremost part of a word is its front, so only opening letters are taken

parts.note: the opening letter
a mote is a tiny speck, as of dust
the opening letter

explanation.surface: A cured ham from Europe's best, speck, is placed alongside smoked hams.
explanation.walkthrough: Speck is also a smoked Tyrolean ham, so the surface is all charcuterie; but 'hams' is a verb meaning overacts.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor who hams overacts theatrically, and one who emotes shows feeling in an exaggerated way.

clue.text: Open venue in New York, finishing with WC Fields?

parts.note: you flush the toilet when you have finished with it
meadows are grassy fields

explanation.surface: A New York venue finishes its season with a comedy by the actor W.C. Fields.
explanation.walkthrough: W.C. Fields was an American comic actor, but the name splits: WC is a toilet, and Fields its own word.
explanation.definitionFit: The US Open tennis championship is held at Flushing Meadows in the borough of Queens.

clue.text: Lower organ, heading off vibration

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its first letter, and off means it is removed

parts.note: a judder, a violent shaking, without its first letter

explanation.surface: A church organ is turned down to stop it shaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lower' reads as reduce, but it is one that lows: a cow, whose organ is the udder. A judder is a shudder.
explanation.definitionFit: A cow lows, so the milk gland of a lowing animal is jokingly its lower organ, and also sits low.

clue.text: Car was leaking endlessly, in condition to be picked up

definitions.text: in condition to be picked up

indicators.note: without an end means the closing letter is cut off

parts.note: Audi is a German car make
bled, meaning lost fluid, with its last letter cut

explanation.surface: A leaking car is fit only to be collected by the breakdown truck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Picked up' suggests collecting the car; here it means heard, as a microphone picks up sound.
explanation.definitionFit: A sound that can be heard or detected by a listener or microphone is capable of being picked up.

clue.text: Glibly repeat, left-winger expelled

parts.note: Trot is short for Trotskyist, a far-left activist
someone expelled is thrown out

explanation.surface: A left-wing party member is expelled for parroting slogans.
explanation.walkthrough: Trot is common British slang for a Trotskyist, a member of the hard left.
explanation.definitionFit: To trot out an excuse or opinion is to produce a stale, familiar line without thought.

clue.text: Dali perhaps not unknown among county celebs

indicators.note: not having something means it is left out of the word

parts.note: Surrey, a county south of London, without the unknown Y
y is an algebraic unknown; this is the letter removed
the A-list is the top tier of celebrities

explanation.surface: Salvador Dali, not an unknown, mixes with the celebrities of the Home Counties.
explanation.walkthrough: In algebra x, y and z are unknowns, so 'unknown' is Y, dropped from Surrey, an English county bordering London.
explanation.definitionFit: Salvador Dali was a leading painter of the Surrealist movement, so he is an example of one.

clue.text: I'm found in transient employment

indicators.note: something found in a place is sitting inside it, so the answer lies within the letters that follow

parts.note: straddles the two words

explanation.surface: A worker introduces themselves as someone in short-term jobs.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition, and the answer also sits across the join of the last two words.
explanation.definitionFit: A temporary worker hired through an agency for short stints is exactly someone in transient employment.
